title: Call it again, and again
idea: TOOL: define a sub-plan once, call it many times; the body runs fresh on each call.

exercises.prompt:
Program:

def line():
    print("----")
line()
line()

What prints?
exercises.explanation: Defined once, called twice, so '----' prints twice. Each call runs the body again.

exercises.prompt: You want a star border above AND below a title. Using def line() that prints stars, the main plan should...
options: call line(), print the title, call line() again
exercises.explanation: Call line() for the top border, show the title, call line() again for the bottom. One def, two calls.

exercises.prompt:
Order a program that frames a title:

(def line already prints '***')
exercises.explanation: Top border, title, bottom border. The single line() sub-plan is reused with two calls.

exercises.prompt: Why is calling the SAME sub-plan twice better than typing the stars twice?
options: One definition to read and fix; both borders stay in sync
exercises.explanation: Change the border once (inside line) and every call updates. Copied code would each need fixing - and drift.

exercises.prompt: If you change the body of line(), every future call to line() shows the new version.
exercises.explanation: Yes. There's one definition. Edit it once and all calls use the updated steps. That's the reuse payoff.

exercises.prompt: A program defines greet() and farewell(), then calls greet(), farewell(). What prints (greet='Hi', farewell='Bye')?
exercises.explanation: Two sub-plans, each called once in order: greet shows 'Hi', farewell shows 'Bye'.

exercises.prompt: Which are TRUE about calling a sub-plan more than once? (Pick all.)
options: The body runs again each call
It was still defined only once
Each call can appear anywhere in the main plan
exercises.explanation: One def, many calls; the body re-runs each call; calls can go anywhere. You do NOT re-define per call.

exercises.prompt: Match each program to how many lines of output it makes (border() prints one line).
exercises.explanation: Each call adds one run of the body. Count the calls to count the output - the def itself prints nothing.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: another tool that repeats the same steps is a loop. A loop vs calling a sub-plan by hand:
options: a loop repeats automatically; calls are placed where you choose
they are identical in every way
exercises.explanation: A loop repeats over a sequence; hand-written calls run the job at the exact spots you pick. Both reuse work.

options: define once, call as many times as you need
exercises.explanation: Write the sub-plan once; call it wherever and however often you need. One source, many runs.
